evidenceKind: primary vendor documentation and local source review; no peer runtime
question: Does a broader semantic-reader search identify a usable external ACIS route, and does the local parser reproduce the peer-reported block-size safety weakness?

sources.observed: The vendor documents a standalone SAT/SAB reader that does not require ACIS installation, R1-2023 input versions, and solid/surface/line body import on Windows and Linux. It does not support CAD associativity or parameters, may skip hidden/suppressed parts, and does not expose a reader save file. Units are read when present or supplied by the user. The page does not expose parser/kernel lineage or a detailed per-SAB-profile matrix.
sources.disposition: OPTIONAL_PROPRIETARY_SEMANTIC_READER_CANDIDATE. Use only if already installed and license-authorized; profile-probe first and record exact build/platform/settings, units, body disposition, validity, topology, and independent analytic metrics. Not a dependency, purchase, blocking gate, open-source peer, DWG reader, or AcDs owner-join oracle. Implementation independence remains provisional.

sources.observed: The commercial component translates SAT/SAB geometry and topology into OCCT shapes and XDE attributes, and documents configurable healing and possible approximation for complex ACIS 5.0+ geometry. Read and write version coverage are separate decisions.
sources.disposition: OPTIONAL COMMERCIAL ROUTE ONLY. It shares the OCCT kernel family with FreeCAD and cq-acis, so it is not an independent-kernel vote. Record exact component, profile, healing/approximation configuration, and changed tolerances if used.

sources.observed: The project describes experimental, profile-dependent SAT/SAB parsing and separates raw parsing from shape conversion; unsupported records may remain raw while failed requested conversions raise. Current mutable README statements do not broaden the existing pinned 0.3.12 profile or its local generated observation.
sources.disposition: Retain existing exact-version/profile gate. No profile, support claim, or semantic verdict is promoted from the mutable README.

references: src/drw_entities.cpp: DRW_ModelerGeometry::parseDwg AC1015 SAT block reader
sources.observed: SAB reads use an index-before-subtraction extent check and separately account parser/graph resource limits. The AC1015 SAT block parser bounds each positive block against cumulative payload capacity and remaining entity-body bytes before reserve/copy. This review found no local equivalent of LibreDWG's reported unchecked 8 * block_size overflow.
sources.disposition: No local defect or test was added. Keep peer overflow and dropped-final-block reports as risk classes; the DXF writer final group-1/group-3 reconstruction remains a distinct existing carrier check. This source-only review did not rerun every writer terminal-chunk case or a sanitizer/fuzz campaign.

implementationReadiness: Continue the local generated S3.7c structural sequence and fast owning target without waiting for an external reader, license, or native platform.
At the existing composed checkpoint, select at most one optional semantic route for an exact admitted payload profile; do not add a package, install, CI lane, or persistent fixture.

Author expected bounds, body/topology counts, volume, and area independently before reading the generated payload; capture profile, carrier hash, reader build, platform, unit choice, skipped/unsupported records, validity, and metric tolerances.
Keep direct bare-SAT/SAB shape evidence separate from DWG section extraction, DataStorage/index/key mapping, entity ownership, DXF carrier reconstruction, and native-consumer qualification.
Treat commercial OCCT ACIS exchange as same-kernel-family corroboration only; record healing/approximation and do not count it as an independent-kernel result.

If authorized external access or exact profile compatibility is absent, record NOT_RUN/DEFERRED_EXTERNAL and self-unblock to local work. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain non-promoting DEFERRED_EXTERNAL items.
limitations: Vendor documentation does not expose Ansys parser/kernel lineage or a complete SAB profile matrix. No external package, proprietary application, or native CAD was installed or run. Local review was limited to the named SAB reader and AC1015 SAT block reader; it did not exhaustively execute all DXF final-chunk writer paths, sanitizers, fuzzers, or platform builds. ODA v5.4.1 remains authoritative for DWG layout.
